### Claude

The consequence is smaller than it sounded. The Terminal was already a special case, and the strip version mostly moves that special case rather than adding a new one.

**Terminal-only code today, before any of this:**
- The ✨ button has its own path for the Terminal in `panes.js` (`if IFRAME`).
- The frame's page has its own copy of the box, plus `GET /inline_box.js` to serve it.
- The frame's page reads the screen, asks the AI and pastes the command.

**With the strip:**
- The ✨ button still has one line just for the Terminal.
- The copy of the box and the route go away; the app's page draws the box, as it does for every other pane.
- New: `terminal_ask.js`, which puts the box in the strip and passes messages to and from the frame.
- The frame's page still does the shell's part.

The cause is that the Terminal is the only pane that's a separate page in a frame. The AI's command has to be typed into the shell inside that frame, so some code has to talk across it either way. The real choice is whether that code is named after the Terminal or after framed panes in general.

**A generic version, at the same cost:** make it a rule for panes, not the Terminal:

- **Spec rule** (`spec/services/ui/README.md`, "Panels"): "A pane whose content has no place of its own for the inline AI box (a framed page) shows it in its title strip, left of ⤢ ×."
- **`ui.py`:** a `strip_ask()` helper any pane can put in its strip; the Terminal is the first user.
- **`assets/frame_ask.js`** (not `terminal_ask.js`): it works with any pane whose content is a frame, and uses generic message names (`delulu-ask-send`, `delulu-ask-answer`, `delulu-ask-paste`).
- **The frame's page** answers those messages. Only the Terminal's page does today; a future framed pane would answer the same ones.

```python
#### ui.py: a pane's strip
def strip_ask() -> rx.Component: ...       # the empty spot frame_ask.js fills; any pane can use it

def terminal_pane():
    head = [strip_ask(), inline_ai_button("iframe", ...), keys_button(...), zoom_button(...), close_button(...)]
```

There's only one framed pane today, so the generic names cost nothing now and only pay off if another one comes along. Either way, it's the same amount of code as the Terminal-named version.

## 15. User

> why is there this black line if i alt+right to the terminal?
>
> *[screenshot]*

### Claude

The thin black line was the browser's own text cursor, not ghostty's. I fixed it with one CSS line in `services/ui/ui/terminal.py`.

- **Cause:** ghostty-web makes the terminal's area an editable element (`contenteditable`). When you click into it, ghostty handles the click itself. But when focus arrives by a key (Alt+Right, or the box closing), the browser shows its own blinking text cursor at the top-left of that area. It drew it in black, because the Terminal's page sets no text colour.
- **Fix:** the browser's cursor and focus outline are now hidden there. ghostty's block cursor is unaffected.

**Checked:** the running backend's Terminal page now has the browser's cursor colour set to transparent and no focus outline. Lint passes. I didn't see the line disappear on screen, because a headless screenshot can't reliably catch a blinking cursor. So check that one yourself.

#### The rule (spec)

A new design rule in `spec/services/ui/README.md`, under the panel / widget rules, so it covers both. It replaces the Panels-table row I added for the Terminal:

> **Toggles don't move the content.** Opening or closing something (a box, a row, a status) never shifts what's already on screen. The inline AI box therefore opens in the title strip of the panel or widget it acts on, taking the strip's free width left of its buttons. **Exception: a console.** A Python cell's box opens under the cell it edits, because the cell is the place the box belongs to.

#### What you'll see

A VODs widget with its inputs open, then ✨ (or Alt+I):

```
Today
│ r1 · vods · 10 VODs                                    ✨ Inputs ▾ ⤢ × │
│ ✨ [Say what the inputs should be, eg: sparg0 vs steve…        ] ×      │  ← pushes the inputs down
│ Player [sparg0]  Opponent [steve]  Sets [90]  Run                        │

Planned
│ r1 · vods · 10 VODs │✨ Say what the inputs should be…  Enter asks AI│ ✨ Inputs ▾ ⤢ × │
│ Player [sparg0]  Opponent [steve]  Sets [90]  Run                        │  ← doesn't move
```

| Moment | In the strip's box | Below it |
|---|---|---|
| Opened | the placeholder as today, hint `Enter asks AI · Esc closes` | the inputs; the form opens if it was folded, as today |
| Thinking | `Thinking…`, with the purple sweep | nothing moves |
| Proposal | placeholder `Enter runs these inputs · or say what else to change · Esc puts the old ones back` | the changed inputs outlined in purple, as today |
| Error | `the request failed: …` in red, cut short, full text on hover | nothing moves |

The box looks exactly like the Terminal's: same classes, same CSS. Closing works as now: Esc, Alt+I, or the lit ✨, which also puts the old inputs back. The row's own × goes away, since the ✨ already does its job.

#### Interfaces

```python
#### render.py: the one strip box for Reflex-drawn strips (a widget's bar). The Terminal's
#### frame_ask.js builds the same markup with inline_box.js, so both look the same.
def strip_ask_box(view: rx.Var[ViewData], send: Any) -> rx.Component:
    """The form's Ask AI input, drawn in the bar. It still belongs to the form through the
    HTML `form=` attribute, so Enter submits the form with the inputs on screen (as today)."""
    return rx.el.div(  # .strip-ask > .inline-box, as frame_ask.js makes
        ai_icon(),
        rx.el.input(name=ASK_FIELD, form=form_id(view), auto_focus=True,
                    key=view.form_key, ...),  # remounts with the form: focus comes back after a proposal
        status(view.ai_busy, view.ai_note, view.ai_error))

def form_id(view) -> rx.Var[str]   # "form-" + the view's slot: ties the bar's box to its form

def _bar(...):                     # the strip
    ..., rx.cond(view.ai_open, strip_ask_box(view, send), spacer), ...

def tool_form(...):                # _ask_row removed; the form gets id=form_id(view)
```

- **`panes.js`:** Esc finds the open box through the widget (`.widget`) instead of `.tool-form`.
- **Unchanged:** `inline_fill.py` and the state events (`ai_toggle`, `ai_discard`, the form submit with `__ask`) keep working as they are.

```python
                              -> inline_fill proposes; the form and the box remount (form_key); the inputs are outlined

```

#### Interfaces: enforced in code

Each widget's render function stops drawing a whole component. It **returns its parts**, and one frame draws everything around them:

```python
#### render.py
@dataclasses.dataclass
class WidgetParts:
    display: rx.Component                     # region 3: the widget's own design
    line: tuple[rx.Component, ...] = ()       # its own controls for the bottom line (Prev/Next, filter, SQL ▸)
    inputs: rx.Component | None = None        # region 2 when it isn't a tool form (the Browser's address)
    ai: rx.Component | None = None            # inline AI with no form (SmashDb's editor ✨)

def widget_frame(view: rx.Var[ViewData], send: Any, parts: WidgetParts,
                 links: tuple[rx.Component, ...]) -> rx.Component:
    """The only place a bar, an Inputs panel or a bottom line is drawn."""
    return rx.el.div(
        bar(view, send, parts.ai),            # name · (ask box | spacer) · ✨ · Inputs · ⤢ · ×
        inputs_panel(view, send, parts.inputs),  # the tool form, or parts.inputs; folds with Inputs ▸/▾
        _error(view),
        rx.el.div(parts.display, class_name="widget-display"),
        bottom_line(view.note, *parts.line, *links))   # links: the place's ↗ tab / ↖ chat

def video_widget(view, send) -> WidgetParts: ...   # every widget function: -> WidgetParts
def render_component(view, on_event, *, compact=False, actions=()):   # same signature; actions -> links
    return widget_frame(view, send, PARTS[view.kind](view, send), actions)
```

**The guard:** a test (`tests/services/ui/test_widget_frame.py`) reads `render.py`. It fails if `bar(`, `float_button(`, `close_view_button(` or `form_section(` is called anywhere but `widget_frame`, or if a widget function doesn't return `WidgetParts`. A new widget then can't draw its own bar.

```python
#### picking a video, list folded
send("play", video) -> display = player (fills the display) + gallery (folded); the bar and Inputs stay as they are
```

#### Edge cases

- **Narrow widgets (chat, cells):** the bar's name never shrinks below a few characters, and the bottom line's note gives way first.
- **A floated widget (⤢):** the whole frame floats, all three regions together.
- **A glance (a clicked link):** a Browser frame like any other, with its Inputs folded, so the page shows first.

#### Decisions for you

1. **The bottom line: always shown** at a fixed height, even when it has nothing in it *(recommended, for consistency)*, or only when it has something to show.
2. **The Browser's Inputs (its address): open while the page is blank, folded once a page is loaded** *(recommended: it behaves like the other Inputs, and a page gets the room)*, or always open.
3. **The guard test** described above *(recommended)*, or no test, with the rule kept by the frame and the spec alone.

I reviewed everything staged from this session (20 files) and the widget-frame plan. Nothing is changed yet. One finding is a real security hole that I'd fix before anything else.

#### Findings in the staged work

| # | Severity | What | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **High** | **Any website open in your browser can type into your shell.** The Terminal's page now accepts a `delulu-ask-paste` message and types its text at the prompt. It only checks that the sender is its parent page, and `/terminal` can be framed by any site. So a hostile page could frame `localhost:8000/terminal` and send it a command (with a newline, possibly run it). Before this session a framing page couldn't send keystrokes at all. | `ui/terminal.py` message handler | Accept messages only from this machine's origins, and send `frame-ancestors` so only the app can frame the page. Add a test. |
| 2 | Medium | **`/clear-all` while the agent works claims it cleared.** Nothing is cleared (correct), but its chat row still says "a new conversation · cleared 3 variables". `/clear-chat` already had the same flaw. | `state._slash_outcome` | The row says "not run: the agent is still working" for both. |
| 3 | Medium | **A late answer steals the cursor.** If you ask in the Terminal's box, move to another pane and keep typing, the answer pulls focus back into the shell, and your keystrokes land there. | `assets/frame_ask.js` `close()` | Only move the cursor to the shell if it was still in the box. |
| 4 | Low | **A lost message.** If a full-screen program (vim, less) starts while the AI is thinking, the command is dropped silently. The old code said "a full-screen program is running; the command was: …". | `terminal.py` / `frame_ask.js` | The page reports back; the box shows the message. |
| 5 | Low | **Double-open race.** Two quick Alt+I presses on the very first open can build two boxes (the first open waits on loading the box's script). | `frame_ask.js` `open()` | Remember the in-flight open. |
| 6 | Low | **The guide is at exactly its 160-line cap**, so the next added line fails a test. | `services/ui/guide.md` | Nothing now; just know it. |

The rest held up on review. I found no problems in the theme reader, the cursor changes, the Ask box in the widget's bar or the shared styles. The `/clear-all` order is right, and the spec text matches what you asked for.

3. **A stronger guard.** Besides the source check, every kind in `WIDGETS` must have an entry in one `PARTS` table (kind to its parts function), and the test fails if one is missing. A new widget can't be added without going through the frame.
